titulo: Composition and depth in the frame
lead: A beautiful frame where the eye doesn't know where to go communicates nothing. Composition is deciding what you see first, where empty space works in your favor, and how foreground, midground and background separate. It's what makes a generated image feel like real space instead of a flat backdrop.
objetivo: compose each frame with a subject you understand in one second and three layers of depth separated by focus, light or color.

aprende.t: Apply the one-second test to any frame
Choose between thirds, center and diagonal by emotion
Use empty space to isolate or squeeze
Set up foreground, midground and background and separate the layers

hero_alt: View from behind a camera monitor showing a frame with a plant in the foreground, a table in the midground and a window in the background.

secoes.sub: Five decisions for every frame. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: What does the audience see first? They shouldn't have to search: they should understand the scene in one second. If two elements compete for attention, one goes or loses light.
Rule of thirds: the subject off-center creates a natural flow from the subject to the setting. Center and symmetry: balance, control, power, ritual.
The diagonal breaks stability and suggests movement, even when still. Leading lines (road, hallway, counter, shadow) lead the eye to the subject.
More empty space: freedom, scale, isolation. Less space: tension, tightness. Emptiness isn't a lack of content; it's the emotional content.
Foreground: where the audience is. Midground: where the subject is. Background: where the context lives. Separate the three by focus, light, color or haze.

secoes.legenda: The composition changes across the sequence: the scene evolves from shot to shot instead of repeating itself.

secoes.sub: The examples come from the bakery.

texto: Look at the frame for one second and say out loud what the subject is. If you hesitate, the audience will hesitate too.
One dominant subject per frame. Product, person and a background detail fighting for attention make a beautiful image that says nothing.

passos.sub: by the emotion of the shot
texto: Thirds for natural flow; center and symmetry for control and monumentality; diagonal for energy and action. The choice follows the emotion of the shot, not taste.
Vary it across the scene: three frames in a row with the same composition feel repetitive.

exemplo.texto: Oven door in the center, symmetrical: the ritual. The row of loaves on a diagonal: the energy of the first batch.

passos.sub: room to breathe or a tight squeeze
texto: Before you generate, decide: should the audience feel room to breathe or a tight squeeze? The amount of emptiness answers that before any other choice.
Dona Lia small in a corner of the frame, with the dark street filling the rest, tells the loneliness of someone who wakes up before the city.

Having foreground, midground and background is not enough: they need to be distinct. Shallow depth of field blurs the foreground or the background; backlight cuts out the subject; color and haze push the background back.
With the layers separated, the sideways camera movement (lesson 3) makes each one move at its own pace, and the space feels real.

secoes.sub: One line per frame: the composition, the three layers and where the eye goes.

exercicios.texto: Write 3 to 6 frames of your scene with the composition, the foreground, the midground, the background and where the eye goes. Use at least 3 different compositions. Check them and download quadros.txt to the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: the page replies OK: [n] frames with composition and three layers to your text and quadros.txt is in the project folder.

exercicios.texto: For each frame, read only the "the eye goes to" line and check that there is just one subject. If the line names two things, take light or focus away from one of them and rewrite it.
exercicios.pronto: in every line of quadros.txt, after o olho vai para:, there is a single subject.

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation shows up after each answer.

opcoes: Generate a one-second clip before the long clip.
Cut each shot to last one second at most.
Glance at the frame and name the subject in one second.
Wait one second of silence before each cut.
perguntas.explica: The audience shouldn't have to hunt for the subject. If you hesitate when saying what the frame shows, the composition failed, however pretty it looks.

perguntas.p: Dona Lia small in the corner, the empty street filling the rest of the frame. What does the empty space say?
opcoes: Haste and urgency in the scene.
That an object is missing from the scene.
perguntas.explica: A lot of negative space isolates the subject and shows how big the world around them is. Little space does the opposite: it squeezes and creates tension.

perguntas.p: How do you separate the subject from the background without changing the composition?
opcoes: Blur the background, add backlight, or change the color.
Put the subject in the exact center of the frame, always.
Fill the background with objects to give context.
Swap the lens for a wide-open wide-angle.
perguntas.explica: Focus, light, color, and fog separate the layers. More objects in the background compete for attention; centering changes the composition; a wide-angle increases the space, but doesn't separate on its own.

perguntas.p: What do symmetry and a centered subject convey?
perguntas.explica: Center and symmetry assert order, monumentality, and control. Energy comes from the diagonal; discomfort, from the Dutch angle; intimacy, from the close-up.

itens.texto: The audience understands the frame in one second, without searching.
Thirds for flow, center for control, diagonal for energy, empty space to isolate.
Foreground, midground, and background, separated by focus, light, color, or fog.
